name: Beyoncé
label: Parkwood/Columbia
lede: Houston talent shows led to a record deal that Elektra dropped before an album came out. Beyoncé has since had eight straight No. 1 debuts, moving from soul to house to country.

eras.title: Houston talent shows, then a father with a clipboard
eras.text: Girl's Tyme rapped on Houston talent circuits and lost on Star Search. Elektra dropped the group before an album, and Mathew Knowles quit his Xerox job to manage it. By 1999 it had a name from the Book of Isaiah and a record headed for the millions.

years.h: Beyoncé meets LaTavia Roberson at a Houston audition
years.p: The audition was for an all-girl group. [[Kelly Rowland|31bea673-d23a-4889-8da1-7cb040863268]] joined in 1992, and the trio worked the local talent circuit as Girl's Tyme.
years.xp: Girl's Tyme rapped and danced its way around Houston. The names that followed were Somethin' Fresh, Cliché, the Dolls, Borderline and, finally, Destiny.

years.h: Girl's Tyme raps on Star Search and loses
years.p: Beyoncé later put the loss down to a poor song choice: the group rapped instead of singing. [[LeToya Luckett|b2f1149b-171a-4bc5-ac8f-3baf9a566abf]] joined around then, making it four.
years.xp:
Producer Arne Frager arranged the Star Search appearance, according to Wikipedia. Beyoncé's father, Mathew Knowles, began managing the group, and Wikipedia dates his exit from a Xerox sales job to 1995.

The Beyoncé and Destiny's Child pages give slightly different years for the Star Search appearance.

q: We got the word destiny out of the Bible, but we couldn't trademark the name, so we added child.
years.h: Dropped by Elektra, Destiny becomes Destiny's Child at Columbia
years.p: Signed as Destiny, the group was cut loose by Elektra before an album appeared. Scout Teresa LaBarbera Whites helped land the renamed group a deal at Columbia.
years.xp: The 1996 name came from a passage in the Book of Isaiah. Beyoncé's fuller explanation, per Wikipedia, was that adding "child" was "like a rebirth of destiny."

yt: Destiny's Child, Say My Name (official video)
years.h: The Writing's on the Wall sells 13 million worldwide
years.p: "Bills, Bills, Bills" was Destiny's Child's first chart-topper, and "Say My Name" followed it to No. 1.

eras.title: A lawsuit, a reshuffle and eleven weeks on top
eras.text: Roberson and Luckett left in a dispute over management, Farrah Franklin came and went, and the trio that remained spent 11 weeks at No. 1. Beyoncé co-wrote and co-produced most of Survivor.

years.h: Williams and Franklin replace Roberson and Luckett
years.p: Roberson and Luckett had tried to leave Mathew Knowles's management in December 1999. Michelle Williams and Farrah Franklin arrived in February 2000.
years.xp:
Roberson and Luckett alleged favoritism toward Beyoncé and Rowland. On March 21, 2000 they sued Knowles and their former bandmates for breach of partnership and fiduciary duties; the case settled in June 2002.

Franklin quit after five months, citing "negativity surrounding the group's internal conflict." That left Beyoncé, Rowland and [[Michelle Williams|fac0f203-eb89-4d34-a3c5-8e353356d756]] as the trio.

years.h: "Independent Women Part I" holds No. 1 into January
years.p: Its 11 weeks at the top, from November 2000 into January 2001, were the longest run of any Destiny's Child chart-topper.

years.h: Beyoncé takes the wheel on Survivor
years.p: She co-wrote and co-produced most of it, and it debuted at No. 1 with 663,000 first-week sales. "Bootylicious" reached No. 2.
years.xp:
The album came out May 1, 2001. Roberson and Luckett filed another suit over the title track, alleging it broke a non-disparagement agreement. Beyoncé's answer: "the lyrics to the single 'Survivor' are Destiny's Child's story because we've been through a lot."

"Bootylicious" made it into the Oxford English Dictionary in 2006. The group announced a hiatus in 2001 to pursue solo projects.

eras.title: Solo first, goodbye second
eras.text: During the hiatus Beyoncé made a solo album that went to No. 1 and won five Grammys. She came back to Destiny's Child once, in 2004, before the group wrapped up.

years.big: "One of the most compelling instruments in popular music."
yt: Crazy in Love ft. Jay-Z (official video)
years.h: Beyoncé goes solo with Dangerously in Love
years.p: "Crazy in Love", with Jay-Z, spent eight weeks at No. 1 before the album debuted there on June 24 with 317,000 first-week sales. That's Jody Rosen of New York Times Style Magazine on her voice.
years.xp: "Baby Boy" stayed at the top for nine weeks. The record won five Grammys at the 46th ceremony in 2004, including Best Contemporary R&B Album, and Wikipedia lists global sales over 11 million.

years.h: One last Destiny's Child album, Destiny Fulfilled
years.p: All three members contributed to the songwriting and served as executive producers. "Lose My Breath" and "Soldier" both reached No. 3.

years.cap: Destiny's Child at Live 8, Philadelphia, July 2, 2005
years.h: Destiny's Child tell a Barcelona crowd it's over
years.p: They said it on stage at the tour stop on June 11, 2005. A farewell show at the NBA All-Star Game in Houston followed on February 19, 2006.
years.xp:
The announcement came at Palau Sant Jordi, in front of about 16,000 people, per Wikipedia.

The greatest-hits set #1's came out in October 2005. Wikipedia counts over 60 million records sold and calls them the best-selling girl group of all time.

eras.title: Birthday record, six Grammys, a break
eras.text: B'Day topped the chart on her 25th birthday, I Am... Sasha Fierce split into ballads and club tracks, and she won six Grammys in one night. Then she stepped away from music.

years.h: B'Day lands on her 25th birthday
years.p: It debuted at No. 1 with 541,000 first-week sales, and "Irreplaceable" sat atop the Hot 100 for ten weeks, the top chart hit of 2007.
years.xp: "Check on It", from The Pink Panther soundtrack, made her the first woman to hold No. 1 with a film and a single at the same time, Wikipedia says. B'Day won Best Contemporary R&B Album at the 49th Grammys.

years.cap: Beyoncé at the MTV Video Music Awards
years.h: I Am... Sasha Fierce gets a ballad half and a club half
years.p: "Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)" was her fifth Hot 100 No. 1 and, Wikipedia says, the first big dance craze of the internet age.
years.xp: "Halo" and "Single Ladies" both went diamond with the RIAA. At the 52nd Grammys in 2010 Beyoncé won six awards, the most won by a woman in one night, according to Wikipedia.
play: Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)

years.h: Nine months off, with stops at the Great Wall and the pyramids
years.p: Beyoncé told the world she would step away from music. Her Essence cover story about the break won a writing award from the New York Association of Black Journalists.
years.xp: The Essence essay was titled "Eat, Play, Love." Museums were on the itinerary too.

eras.title: No manager, no warning
eras.text: After her father stopped managing her in 2011, everything ran through her own company. In December 2013 an album showed up on iTunes with no announcement.

years.h: 4 is her first album through her own company, Parkwood
years.p: Mathew Knowles stopped managing her in March 2011. The record went to No. 1 in June, her fourth straight.

years.h: Beyoncé headlines Glastonbury's Pyramid Stage
years.p: She was the first solo woman in more than two decades to headline it, two days after 4 came out.

years.cap: Beyoncé with Kelly Rowland and Michelle Williams, Super Bowl XLVII halftime show, New Orleans, February 2013
yt: Beyoncé and Destiny's Child, Super Bowl XLVII halftime
years.h: Destiny's Child reunite at Beyoncé's Super Bowl halftime show
years.p: Rowland and Williams joined her on stage in New Orleans. It became the second most tweeted-about moment in history at the time, at 268,000 tweets per minute.

years.h: Beyoncé drops a visual album on iTunes with no warning
years.p: Beyoncé, her fifth studio album, debuted at No. 1 with 617,000 first-week sales and passed a million downloads in six days. The videos had been recorded in secret.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits the release with pushing the industry's global release day to Friday, adopted by the IFPI.

"Drunk in Love", with Jay-Z, peaked at No. 2 and won two Grammys. The album explores marriage, motherhood, postnatal depression and bulimia, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Events, not albums
eras.text: Each release arrived as a TV special, a film or a festival headline, and each set the next one's bar.

years.h: "Formation" drops, then Beyoncé plays it at Super Bowl 50
years.p: The halftime set drew controversy over perceived Black Panther Party allusions.

years.cap: Beyoncé on the Formation World Tour, May 2016
years.h: Lemonade premieres on HBO and Tidal the same night
years.p: An hour-long film on HBO, the album exclusive to Tidal. It debuted at No. 1 with 653,000 first-week sales, her sixth straight, and all 12 tracks charted on the Hot 100.
years.xp:
Scholar Emily J. Lordi called it "a cinematic and sonic Afrodiasporic journey from betrayal to redemption."

"Sorry", "Hold Up", "Freedom" and "All Night" were singles. The Formation World Tour ran April to October 2016 and was the first all-stadium tour by a woman, Wikipedia says. She won eight awards at that year's MTV VMAs, including Video of the Year for "Formation", and Lemonade took Best Urban Contemporary Album at the 2017 Grammys.

years.h: Coachella gets HBCU marching bands and a Destiny's Child cameo
years.p: Critics called the April 14 set historic, and it became the most-watched live performance on YouTube up to then. She played two weekends.
years.xp:
The show paid homage to Black culture and HBCUs, per Wikipedia. Rowland and Williams came on for the Destiny's Child moment.

The film Homecoming reached Netflix on April 17, 2019, with a live album, and earned six Emmy nominations.

years.h: Beyoncé and Jay-Z release a joint album as the Carters
years.p: Everything Is Love arrived on June 16, partway through their On the Run II tour. It debuted at No. 2 with 123,000 album-equivalent units; "Apeshit" reached No. 13.

years.h: Beyoncé voices Nala and curates The Lion King: The Gift
years.p: She worked with African producers and folded in gqom and Afrobeat. The visual companion Black Is King followed in July 2020.

eras.title: Disco, house and a leak
eras.text: After the pandemic Beyoncé turned to disco and house, the music of Black queer clubs, as the first part of a trilogy. Critics were nearly unanimous: 91 on Metacritic.

years.h: Beyoncé becomes the most-awarded singer in Grammy history
years.p: She led the 63rd Grammys with nine nominations and won four, which Wikipedia puts second overall among all people.

years.h: "Break My Soul" is her eighth Hot 100 No. 1
years.p: She announced Renaissance on June 16 and dropped the lead single four days later. It held No. 1 for two weeks.

years.cap: Beyoncé on the Renaissance World Tour, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London
years.h: Renaissance scores 9.0 at Pitchfork and tops its 2022 list
years.p: Pitchfork's Julianne Escobedo Shepherd called it a "challenging, densely-referenced album." Metacritic gives it 91 from 26 reviews.
years.xp:
Producers include The-Dream, Honey Dijon, Skrillex, Mike Dean and Hit-Boy. Grace Jones, Tems and Beam feature, and samples include Big Freedia, Right Said Fred, Robin S. and the Clark Sisters.

Copies went to French retailers early on July 27, and the album leaked before its July 29 release. It topped 25 publications' year-end lists. All 16 tracks charted on the Hot 100, and "Cuff It" peaked at No. 6 and became her longest-charting single.

years.h: Beyoncé drops "spaz" from "Heated" after objections
years.p: Disability advocates called the word an ableist slur. Beyoncé announced on August 1 that it would be replaced with "blast".
years.xp: Wikipedia's page on the song notes some listeners said the word means something different in African-American English, but advocates held to the objection. Kelis also objected to the interpolation of "Milkshake" on "Energy".

eras.title: Stadiums, then Americana
eras.text: She took Renaissance around the world, then turned to country. The Grammys answered with Album of the Year.

years.cap: Beyoncé on the Renaissance World Tour, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London, June 1, 2023
years.h: The Renaissance World Tour clears $579 million
years.p: It ran from May to October 2023 and is the highest-grossing tour by a woman and by a Black artist. A concert film followed.
years.xp:
She also won four of her nine nominations at the 65th Grammys, including Best Dance/Electronic Album for Renaissance, bringing her career total to 32 and making her the most-awarded artist in Grammy history, Wikipedia says.

Wikipedia's Beyoncé page dates the film to November 2023, its album page to December 1.

years.h: Cowboy Carter turns to country, and to the Black artists it overlooked
years.p: "Texas Hold 'Em" gave her a ninth Hot 100 No. 1 before release. The album debuted at No. 1 with 407,000 first-week sales, her eighth in a row.
years.xp: "II Most Wanted", with Miley Cyrus, debuted at No. 6. The Cowboy Carter Tour became the highest-grossing country tour ever, Wikipedia says.

years.h: Cowboy Carter wins Album of the Year and Best Country Album
years.p: She was the first Black artist to win Best Country Album, and the first Black woman in 26 years to take Album of the Year.

years.h: "Morning Dew (Donk)" appears without warning
years.p: The surprise single leads a 20th-anniversary edition of B'Day with unreleased tracks, which followed on September 4, 2026.

sources.title: PopBase on X: Pitchfork gives Renaissance 9.0
